newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIA EAGER TO RESTART LEAGUE PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIA EAGER TO RESTART LEAGUE PROGRAMME.

text.p: Albania's soccer federation, eager to restart its league suspended as armed anarchy swept the nation earlier this year, staged a series of friendlies in Tirana on Wednesday.
Gjergj Thaka, a senior federation official, said the Friendship Cup was initiated in a bid to resurrect the 18-team national league which was suspended in January.
Some 500 fans stood for a minute's silence before the three matches in a tribute to the 300 people killed since the uprising began.
Clubs from Tirana, the central town of Kavaje, the southern town of Fier and the northern town of Shkoder took part in the cup at the Qemal Stafa stadium.
The federation plans to resume the national league next month by staging matches under police control.

The league was suspended amid protests over the collapse of investment schemes in which many Albanians had deposited savings. The protests spilled over into armed rebellion last month following the collapse of the get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes.
Seventeen rounds of the league remain in the 1996-97 season.
Soccer officials said 12 of 19 players in the national under-21 squad had sought asylum in other European countries after games against Ukraine and Germany in Spain.
